claims.text: No dedicated gluten-free kitchen or cross-contamination protocol is published. Classic French preparations routinely use wheat flour in sauces, pastry, and coatings.
No mention of tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternatives. French-Japanese fusion cooking at this level commonly incorporates regular soy sauce (which contains wheat) in marinades and sauces.
Animal products (butter, cream, meat stocks, seafood) are central to the cuisine; vegan cross-contact is highly probable given the 10-seat kitchen with no vegan-specific protocol.
The restaurant explicitly requires allergy and dietary restriction disclosure at the time of reservation ('ご予約時にアレルギーなどNG食材を必ずお伝えください'). Same-day menu changes are not accepted.
Pre-reservation allergy declaration policy means the chef is made aware of restrictions before cooking begins, giving the best chance of accommodation within a French tasting-menu format.
Soba is cooked alongside udon and ramen in a small kitchen; shared boiling water and utensils make wheat cross-contamination very likely.
No tamari or GF soy sauce is mentioned; standard wheat-containing soy sauce is used in the tsuyu and dashi, as is universal practice at this type of conventional soba-ya.
Broth is fish-based (katsuo/niboshi dashi standard for this style); no plant-based broth alternative is offered.
Karaage (wheat-battered fried chicken) is a standard lunch item, indicating a shared fryer environment with no GF separation.
Kissaten cooking in Japan routinely uses wheat-containing soy sauce in marinades and dressings; no tamari or GF soy sauce alternatives are indicated.
Eggs, dairy (butter on toast), and animal broths are integral to every service period; no vegan separation possible.
鉄板焼きでは同一の調理面を複数の食材・ソースに使用するため、小麦を含む醤油ベースのソース等との接触リスクがある。グルテンへの配慮に関する記載は公式サイト・予約サイトのいずれにも見当たらない。
鉄板料理のタレや仕上げには醤油（小麦含有）が一般的に使われる。グルテンフリー醤油（丸大豆醤油等）の使用に関する明示はない。
全コースが和牛・魚介を中心に構成されており、同一の鉄板面での交差接触は避けられない構造。ヴィーガン向けの分離調理に関する案内は確認できない。
公式サイトは「ご予算・ご要望に合わせてコースをご用意」と記載しており、アレルギー等の事前申告は予約時に電話で確認することを推奨。英語対応は未確認。
完全予約制かつ少人数対応の個室あり。食材は予約ごとに個別調達するスタイルで、事前に詳細な要望を伝えやすい環境。

name: レイヤーズ 丸の内 本店 (LAYER'S Marunouchi Honten)

claims.text: No dedicated gluten-free fryer or preparation area is documented. Wheat buns are central to every menu item and the kitchen is a standard burger operation.
Sauce ingredients (BBQ, teriyaki, chili variants) are not publicly disclosed; teriyaki sauce in Japanese kitchens typically contains wheat-based soy sauce.
All patties are beef; cheese is standard on most burgers. No plant-based items exist to assess cross-contact.
Standard ramen kitchen with no GF protocols noted; wheat noodles cooked in shared water, wheat-based soy sauce used in broth.
Shoyu (soy sauce) variety uses conventional soy sauce which contains wheat. No tamari or wheat-free soy sauce alternative mentioned on any source.
Entire menu is built around pork-bone and seafood broth; no plant-based option exists, so cross-contact is total and unavoidable.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (shoyu) contains wheat; this is the defining flavor of the broth. No wheat-free soy sauce alternative is offered.

The soy sauce kaeshi is described as Aichi Prefecture tamari soy sauce blended with multiple other soy sauces. Tamari is typically wheat-free but the full blend is unconfirmed; wheat content cannot be ruled out.
